title: Buckaroo Bowl II
dek: Buckaroo Bowl II was the 2024 championship of the Buckaroo Football League, a two-week total over NFL weeks 17 and 18 in which Kaushal's top-seeded Habibsters beat Ramon's Araleasers 261.44-145.28 to win a second straight title.
body: Buckaroo Bowl II decided the 2024 championship of the Buckaroo Football League, then a six-team league in its second season. It was played as a two-week total across NFL weeks 17 and 18 and matched the Habibsters, managed by Kaushal, against the Araleasers, managed by Ramon.

The Habibsters entered as the No. 1 seed after an 11-3 regular season in which they scored 1,524.8 points. Kaushal was the defending champion, having won Buckaroo Bowl I in 2023, and Luffy gave the Habibsters a 93% chance to win the title before kickoff. It was about as close to a coronation as a fantasy projection gets.

The Araleasers arrived as the No. 3 seed with a 7-7 record and 1,430.9 points, roughly 94 fewer than their opponent. Ramon had no earlier titles, and Luffy rated Brucie's chances at 7%. A .500 team reaching the final was already a plot twist; winning it would have required a much bigger one.

The teams had met three times in the regular season. The Araleasers won the first meeting 112.46-102.24 in week 2, but the Habibsters took the next two decisively, 122.26-69.42 in week 7 and 111.76-56.4 in week 12. Habib had beaten Ramon by a combined 108.2 points across those last two games, a trend the championship would extend.

The Habibsters reached the final by beating Alan's Team Pillbert 296.96-245.08 in a two-week semifinal over weeks 15 and 16. Brian Thomas Jr. led the way with 51.2 points, and the Habibsters' 296.96 was a total Philly could not keep pace with despite putting up 245.08 of his own.

The Araleasers advanced past Randy's The fumblers 202.44-176.14 over the same two weeks. Josh Allen carried Ramon's team with 52.4 points, a fitting performance for a Chicago-born manager whose loyalties had drifted to Buffalo. The 26.3-point margin was comfortable, though Ramon's semifinal total was nearly 95 points below what Kaushal's team had posted in the other bracket.
No play-by-play exists for Buckaroo Bowl II; the league site did not begin saving in-game events until week 7 of 2026, so the order of scoring within each week is not recorded.

Week 17: The Habibsters opened with 138.8 points to the Araleasers' 87.5, building a 51.3-point lead after the first half of the matchup. Patrick Mahomes posted 26 points, Ladd McConkey 25.4, Jahmyr Gibbs 24.3 and Brian Thomas Jr. 20.4 for Kaushal. Ramon got 25.7 from Mike Evans, 23.3 from Bijan Robinson, 23 from Josh Allen and 18.4 from Travis Kelce, but the Cowboys D/ST finished at -4 and Jayden Reed managed 1.1.

Week 18: Any hope of a comeback faded quickly. The Habibsters added 122.6 points while the Araleasers scored 57.8, the lowest weekly total by either side in the game. Gibbs produced 43.5 points in the week, more than three-quarters of Ramon's entire week 18 output on his own. Robinson's 30.3 was the Araleasers' lone bright spot, and Allen and Kelce were credited with no points in the second week.

The Habibsters won 261.44-145.28. The 116.2-point margin was larger than the Araleasers' week 18 score and their week 17 score, so the final second half added 64.9 points to a lead that was already out of reach.

Jahmyr Gibbs was the game's standout, scoring 67.8 points against a two-week projection of 42.2. He had averaged 17.9 points per start for the Habibsters during the season, and his 43.5 in week 18 alone more than doubled that rate. Ladd McConkey added 39.4 points against a 23.9 projection, a big jump from the 8.7 per start he had averaged in three earlier starts for the team.

Kaushal's supporting cast largely held to form. Brian Thomas Jr. scored 34.2 (projected 31.2), Sam LaPorta 25.2 (projected 19.4, and far above his 4.5 per-start average), J.K. Dobbins 23.8, D'Andre Swift 22.6, Nico Collins 19.7 and kicker Jake Elliott 18. The underperformers were Justin Jefferson, who scored 20.1 against a projection of 36, Sam Darnold at 7.6 against 20.6 in week 18, and the Chiefs D/ST, whose -8 in week 18 left it at 3 points for the game against a 10.8 projection.

For the Araleasers, Bijan Robinson scored 53.6 points against a 38.6 projection, well above his 16.1 per-start season average, and Mike Evans added 39.1 against a projection of 26.8. Travis Kelce's 18.4 came entirely in week 17 and beat his 10.5 projection. The rest of the lineup struggled: Jayden Reed scored 5.2 against a projection of 20, and Greg Zuerlein scored 0 against 7.1.

Alvin Kamara and David Montgomery were each in the Araleasers' starting lineup with projections of zero and scored zero in both weeks. Meanwhile Ramon's bench held DeVonta Smith's 27 points, Najee Harris's 22.7, Calvin Ridley's 20.4 and James Cook's 20.1. Even replacing Kamara, Montgomery and Zuerlein with Smith, Harris and Brandon Aubrey (14) would have added 63.7 points, a little more than half the 116.2-point margin, so no lineup reshuffle would have changed the result. On the other side, Bucky Irving's 15.4 bench points in week 18 went unused by Habib and were not needed.

The victory made Kaushal the league's first repeat champion and the only manager to have won two Buckaroo Bowls, after titles in Bowl I (2023) and Bowl II (2024). His Habibsters finished 1st of 6, and the result matched Luffy's 93% pregame confidence almost to the letter. Two seasons in, every championship ring in the league belonged to Habib.

The Araleasers finished 2nd of 6, the best finish in Ramon's history to that point and the closest Brucie had come to a title. The game also ended a season in which Ramon took a .500 team to the final, a run that the league would remember next to what came the following year, when he was removed for inactivity after week 8 of 2025.

At the other end of the standings, Sonny's Ben Dover finished last in 2024 for the second straight season, losing the consolation ladder again. That made the 2024 season bookended by a repeat champion and a repeat Bum Bowl loser. Sonny's turnaround came the next year, when Ben Dover went 13-3 and won Buckaroo Bowl III in 2025, ending Kaushal's two-year hold on the trophy.
